questions.q: A stakeholder asks why one specific customer was flagged as likely to churn. What kind of explanation answers that?
options: A global explanation
An intrinsic explanation
A validation explanation
A local explanation
questions.explain: A local explanation describes why a single prediction came out the way it did; a global explanation describes model behavior overall.

questions.q: What distinguishes an intrinsic model from a post-hoc explanation method?
options: An intrinsic model, like logistic regression, can be read directly; post-hoc methods explain an already-trained black box
Intrinsic models are always less accurate
Post-hoc methods change the trained model's predictions
Intrinsic explanations only work on images
questions.explain: Intrinsic (interpretable) models expose their logic through structure such as coefficients. Post-hoc methods like permutation importance and SHAP are applied after training.

questions.q: A churn model's AUC jumps from 0.71 to 0.95 after adding a cancel_call_30d column, which carries 88% of the importance. What is the most likely conclusion?
options: The model has become dramatically better and should ship
The column is a leak: it happens because the customer is leaving and would not be available at prediction time
Gradient boosting always behaves this way
The test set is too small to trust any metric
questions.explain: A feature that is a consequence of the outcome makes metrics look great but is useless in production. The importance ranking exposed it.

questions.q: In the lesson's example, logistic regression scored AUC 0.741 and default gradient boosting 0.706. What does this illustrate?
options: Logistic regression is always better than boosting
AUC values below 0.75 are meaningless
A more complex black-box model is not automatically more accurate, so an interpretable model is worth trying
Boosting cannot be used on churn data
questions.explain: Results depend on the data. Here the readable model won, which is a good reason to benchmark simple, interpretable models first.

questions.q: Which is the best-supported statement about regulation and explainability?
options: Some decisions about people, such as lending, may require reasons, but requirements vary so check with legal and compliance
No regulation anywhere cares how models make decisions
Every model in every industry must use SHAP
Explainability is only needed for image models
questions.explain: Requirements differ by country and industry. Do not assume; confirm with legal and compliance teams.
